metrics.description: The proportion of Trojan nodes correctly identified out of the total number of Trojan nodes in the ground truth.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: The proportion of reported suspect nodes that are not part of the Trojan logic.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: The wall-clock time taken by the analysis script to produce the report, measured in seconds.
metrics.name: inference_latency

acceptance_criteria: The submitted report correctly identifies trojan_detected as true.
The suspect_nodes list contains the exact hierarchical name of the trigger cone's output net and the payload gate that drives the suppressed clock enable signal.
The suspect_nodes list does not contain any false positives (nodes unrelated to the Trojan).
hidden_spec.ground_truth: A rare four-input NAND cone drives the labeled enable mask; when active it forces update_en low and freezes the authentication state register.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check if the submitted suspect_nodes list includes the hierarchical name of the output net of the 4-input NAND gate that forms the trigger.
security_requirements.requirement: The detection method must identify the rare trigger cone composed of a four-input NAND gate with specific net connections.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check if the submitted suspect_nodes list includes the hierarchical name of the gate that drives the update_en net low when the trigger is activated.
security_requirements.requirement: The detection method must identify the payload gate that suppresses the clock enable signal.

hidden_spec.threat_model: A denial-of-service Trojan freezes security state updates while leaving combinational outputs apparently normal.

constraints: The netlist is a flat, synthesized gate-level Verilog file using cells from the provided standard cell library.
The design contains a finite state machine and a register bank with a shared clock enable.
The netlist includes a rare trigger cone implemented with primitive gates and a payload that affects the clock enable signal.
The normal data outputs of the design remain functionally correct as long as the trigger condition is not met.
The analysis must be performed on the provided netlist; no modifications to the netlist are permitted.
expected_outputs: A valid trojan_report.json file in the submission directory.
The report must contain a top-level 'trojan_detected' boolean field.
The report must contain a 'suspect_nodes' list of strings, where each string is a hierarchical netlist node name.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted trojan_report.json must be valid JSON and parseable by a standard JSON parser.
The 'trojan_detected' field must be a boolean value (true or false).
The 'suspect_nodes' field must be a list of strings. Each string must match the exact hierarchical name of a wire or gate instance in the provided netlist.

public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided gate-level netlist and identify any suspicious logic that could interfere with the correct operation of the design. Submit a report listing all suspect nodes and a classification of the overall netlist.
public_spec.response_format:
A JSON object with the following fields:
- trojan_detected (boolean): true if any Trojan is present, false otherwise.
- suspect_nodes (list of strings): A list of hierarchical node names in the netlist that are part of the Trojan logic. An empty list is acceptable if trojan_detected is false.
